To enhance immersion and interactivity with CMS data, we have developed a virtual reality (VR) software package named CEDVR (for CMS Event Display in Virtual Reality) that uses widely-available VR headsets and hand controllers. This application provides an immersive detector-coordinate view and a novel, complementary LEGO-style view. CEDVR provides easy access to physics object properties and object filtering, and incorporates novel VR features for navigation and object selection. Compatible with consumer-grade Quest headsets, CEDVR is a useful visualization tool for CMS physicists, and contains built-in sample events that support educational and public outreach initiatives.

title: Analytic response functions of space-based gravitational-wave detectors to ultralight scalar-field dark matter under multiple types of TDI combinations
summary: Ultralight scalar fields are important candidates for dark matter. As coherently oscillating fields, they can leave characteristic signatures in space-based gravitational-wave detectors through their coupling to test masses. In this paper, we derive analytic expressions for the response functions of space-based gravitational-wave detectors to ultralight scalar-field dark matter under multiple types of time-delay interferometry (TDI) combinations. Starting from the coupling action between the scalar field and a test mass, we obtain the additional displacement of the test mass and the single-link Doppler response. We then give the general analytic form of the response function for an arbitrary TDI combination and compare the analytic and Monte Carlo numerical results for the optimal combinations A, E, and T. Finally, we analyze the responses of multiple types of TDI combinations, classify them into ordinary and ζ types according to their low-frequency behavior, and give the low-frequency response expressions of the individual combinations. The results can be used to evaluate the sensitivity of space-based gravitational-wave missions such as LISA, Taiji, and TianQin to the mass and coupling parameters of ultralight scalar-field dark matter.

title: Obstructions to Hadamard Deformations of Fourier Matrices
summary:
We study deformations of the Fourier spin model commuting square in the space of commuting squares, or equivalently deformations of the matrix $\sqrt nF_n$, where $F_n$ denotes the Fourier matrix, by complex Hadamard matrices. If $n$ is neither a prime power nor twice a prime, we show that there exist unit vectors in the enveloping tangent space that cannot be realized as directions of convergence of sequential deformations.
  Consequently, the derivative of any differentiable Hadamard family through $\sqrt nF_n$ has rank strictly smaller than the dimension of the enveloping tangent space at $\sqrt nF_n$ (i.e., the defect of $F_n$). This is particularly surprising because for every $n$ there exist enough one-parameter analytic families to provide a basis of directions in the enveloping tangent space.
  We obtain cubic obstructions when $n$ has at least three distinct prime divisors, quartic obstructions when it has exactly two and a repeated factor, and quintic obstructions when it is the product of two distinct odd primes. These results extend our order $30$ result from \cite{HN}.

title: Ground state and thermal phase diagrams of the magnetized spin-$1/2$ XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice
summary: The spin-1/2 XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice in a magnetic field is a paradigmatic frustrated quantum magnet, yet its ground-state phase diagram at generic anisotropy and its thermal phase structure remain incompletely understood. Here, using infinite density-matrix renormalization group, infinite projected entangled-pair operator, and exponential tensor renormalization group methods, supported by exact diagonalization, we resolve both issues. At zero temperature, we map the phase diagram continuously from the Ising limit to the Heisenberg point and find that the nonclassical $Ψ$ supersolid is a stable phase just below saturation at all anisotropies studied: it borders the one-third-magnetization up-up-down plateau directly in the strongly easy-axis regime and the semiclassical $V$ phase toward the Heisenberg point. In the strongly easy-axis regime, we uncover an intrinsically finite-temperature bond-nematic phase above the zero-temperature plateau--$Ψ$ boundary, in which the three bond directions become spontaneously inequivalent without transverse spin coherence or three-sublattice order. A hard-core-boson mapping reveals its origin: once thermal fluctuations destroy phase coherence, the field-doped holes settle on domain walls of the local up-up-down order, which are stabilized by quantum kink delocalization and aligned by its $Z_3$ registry. Our results call for reexamining high-field states in triangular-lattice cobaltates such as Na$_2$BaCo(PO$_4$)$_2$ and K$_2$Co(SeO$_3$)$_2$.

title: The Matrix in Pieces: Complete BFSS Scattering at Finite Rank
summary: As two matrix blocks separate in Banks-Fischler-Shenker-Susskind matrix quantum mechanics, the modes connecting them develop a growing excitation gap. Supersymmetry cancels their leading vacuum energy, so blocks in internal bound states can scatter as composite particles. We prove that these particle channels are asymptotically complete for the physical relative Hamiltonian at each fixed finite rank $N\ge 2$. Because a block can itself break up as its center moves away from the others, the proof must control motion on both scales. Inverse powers of the matrix radius control derivatives along internal flat directions, while the growing gap suppresses excitations between blocks. Propagation estimates then allow us to resolve successive breakups by induction on the block rank. The incoming and outgoing wave operators each have range equal to the absolutely continuous subspace, and the singular-continuous subspace vanishes. The scattering operator is thus unitary when each constituent can occupy any of its internal bound states. For a normalized incoming state of zero-energy constituents, the outgoing probability missing from the zero-energy channels equals the inclusive probability of producing at least one constituent with positive internal energy.

title: Background characterization in the PIKACHU Phase 1 search for two-neutrino double-beta decay of $^{160}$Gd
summary:
We report a background characterization for the search for two-neutrino double-beta ($2
u2β$) decay of $^{160}$Gd using Ce:Gd$_3$Al$_2$Ga$_3$O$_{12}$ scintillators in the PIKACHU experiment Phase 1 at the Kamioka underground laboratory. The experimental backgrounds were investigated through delayed-coincidence analysis and spectral fitting based on GEANT4 simulations. In particular, surface contamination of the crystal was identified through the characteristic distortion of the $^{214}$Po $α$-ray spectrum, leading to an improved background model that reproduces the observed energy spectra. No significant excess attributable to $^{160}$Gd $2
u2β$ decay was observed, yielding a lower limit of $T^{2ν}_{1/2} \geq 2.32 	imes 10^{19}$ yr at 90\% C.L. The established background model and analysis framework provide a foundation for future PIKACHU phases aiming to discover $^{160}$Gd $2
u2β$ decay.

title: Toward Solving the Galactic Foreground Problem in Gravitational-Wave Astronomy with Machine Learning
summary: Space-borne gravitational-wave detectors will see tens of millions of Galactic binaries. Resolved, they would form a census of the Galaxy's ultracompact binaries unhindered by dust; unresolved, they are the dominant noise up to a few millihertz for massive black-hole binaries, extreme-mass-ratio inspirals and backgrounds from the early Universe. Separating the two requires the number of binaries, which is ill-defined because binaries exist at every amplitude. We make it an observable by defining a source as a binary above a signal-to-noise threshold. Neural flows count the binaries to within one in 99% of 1 microhertz intervals over 0.5-10 mHz, and nested sampling resolves them, even pairs closer than one frequency bin. The data themselves set a limit: a source is resolvable only if its signal pays for its own description, about 20 nats, which biases even ideal trans-dimensional samplers. Like the diffraction limit in imaging, this Bayesian confusion limit is set by the data rather than by the method, and it governs any superposition of weak sources, from radio surveys and pulsar timing arrays to super-resolution microscopy. For future space-borne detectors, the method turns the Galactic foreground into a definite, calibrated count of binaries with an analytic selection function, the basis for global fits and for tests of population models.

title: Morphogenic necking of surfaces
summary: Surface morphogenesis occurs across biological scales, from subcellular vesicles and cells to visceral organs, tissue organoids, and whole organisms. Since morphogenesis often involves changes in topology, a natural question is that of appropriate mathematical descriptions that provide an approach to topological transitions of thin surfaces. Here, we suggest a general intrinsic framework coupling morphogen organization to surface geometry. We propose a minimal geometric model in which smoothing competes with morphogen-induced deformation to regulate shape, while loss of this balance can bring a surface toward a topological transition via neck constriction. A simple dynamical model coupling a scalar field to the surface metric reveals two mechanisms: gradient-driven constriction at steep morphogen transitions and curvature-driven constriction near localized morphogen peaks. For frozen morphogen profiles in simple axisymmetric examples, the gradient-driven route gives exact algebraic contraction, while the curvature-driven route gives local exponential contraction.

title: Strain-enabled dynamical magnetoelectric coupling in BaFe$_{12}$O$_{19}$
summary: Optical excitation has emerged as a powerful tool for manipulating and creating non-equilibrium phases of matter. Yet, the pathways available for optical control are intrinsically limited by the symmetries and interactions of the equilibrium system. Here, we demonstrate that these pathways can be redesigned through atomic-structural engineering to access hidden dynamical properties. By combining resonant vibrational excitation with epitaxial strain, we realize a light-induced, room-temperature multiferroic state in strained thin films of the technologically relevant hexagonal ferrimagnet, barium hexaferrite (BaFe$_{12}$O$_{19}$, BaM). Time-resolved second harmonic generation and magneto-optical Kerr effect measurements reveal an enhanced ferroelectric polarization together with a weakening of the magnetic moment upon exciting mid-infrared phonons in strained BaM thin films, but not in the bulk material. Structural analysis and first-principles-based theory show that this effect is enabled by strain-generated displacement of Fe$^{3+}$ ions, which break the local symmetry and facilitate an emergent dynamical magnetoelectric coupling. Both the strong lattice excitation and strain-induced symmetry breaking are essential for enabling this dynamical coupling, promising an important template for designing otherwise inaccessible non-equilibrium phenomena.

title: Second-order localization and intersecting O6-planes in scale-separated AdS vacua
summary: We construct explicit periodic second-order localization corrections to scale-separated AdS$_4$ vacua of massive type IIA supergravity on $T^6/(\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2)$. At first order, the corrections from different O6-plane families simply add. The interactions between intersecting families first enter at second order and could obstruct the continuation of the solution. We find explicit solutions for the warp factor, dilaton, full internal metric and required form fields, including the terms generated by these interactions. The metric at second order contains off-diagonal components. With a common regularization of the singular source terms, we verify the full field equations and the conditions required for a solution on a compact space. Using the pure-spinor formalism, we find that the second-order fields satisfy the supersymmetry conditions accessible at the retained orders.

title: Studies of dual ions arriving time reconstruction in N$ν$DEx time projection chamber
summary:
The N$ν$DEx experiment aims to search for neutrinoless double-beta decay of \(^{82}\)Se with a high-pressure \(^{82}\)SeF\(_6\) negative-ion time projection chamber. In the assumed two-carrier model, the arrival-time separation of SeF\(_5^-\) and SeF\(_6^-\) can estimate the longitudinal coordinate without an external trigger. We compare FFT deconvolution and direct waveform fitting on simulated Topmetal-S charge-sensitive-amplifier waveforms.
  With the fixed amplifier response, direct fitting and FFT accepted 873 and 855 of 873 geometry-selected single depositions, respectively. On the 855 common events, the arrival-time separation RMSEs were 0.180 and 0.222 ms. Numerical depth calibration gave mean \(z\) residuals of 0.036 and 0.075 cm and RMSEs of 0.192 and 0.208 cm on 848 common events. With sampled CSA shaping, FFT accepted the same 855 waveforms and direct fitting accepted 866 of 873. On the four-way common sample of 855 events, the direct-fit separation RMSE was 0.180~ms with fixed shaping and 0.217~ms with sampled shaping. An accepted near-readout direct fit outside the FFT sample had a 184~ms separation error, giving an RMSE of 6.25~ms over all accepted sampled-response direct fits.
  With the fixed response, the full-track fit retained 1,185 of 1,810 observed pads in 100 selected Geant4 events. The median event-level depth RMSE was 0.184 cm. Subtracting each event's mean Monte Carlo residual gave a median event-centred RMS of 0.102 cm as a diagnostic of relative track shape. The absolute depth remains sensitive to the common event time. Validation with detector data is needed to assess the effects of diffusion, electronics noise, and inter-pad response.

title: An uncalibrated effective-one-body waveform model for intermediate-mass-ratio black hole binaries
comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables, plus 3 pages of Supplemental Material (1 figure, 2 tables)
summary: Intermediate-mass-ratio binaries, with mass ratios $q=m_1/m_2\sim10^2-10^4$, are among the most challenging sources for waveform modeling. We present an inspiral-merger-ringdown effective-one-body model for nonspinning, quasicircular binaries with $q>10$, with dynamics built only from analytical post-Newtonian results. It reaches $(2,2)$ unfaithfulness of $10^{-4}-10^{-5}$ against numerical-relativity simulations with $q>10$ and subradian dephasing against second-order self-force waveforms over four-year inspirals at $q=10^4-10^5$. An optimized post-adiabatic implementation enables waveform generation up to two orders of magnitude faster than integrating the full equations of motion.

title: Free hyperboloidal evolution in 3D: gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves
summary: Hyperboloidal evolution allows to reach future null infinity within numerical relativity simulations. This work extends the conformal compactification approach with BSSN/Z4 from spherical symmetry to full 3D simulations. This is the first free numerical hyperboloidal evolution in 3D with a common formulation of general relativity. In this first step, gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves perturbing Minkowski spacetime are evolved nonlinearly and show that the implementation is reliable and signals can be successfully extracted at future null infinity.

title: Moiré-enabled polariton control in large-angle twisted bilayer graphene
summary: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is commonly viewed through two limiting regimes: strongly correlated flat bands near the magic angle and nearly decoupled Dirac cones at large twist angles. Here we explore the intermediate regime. Using hyperbolic plasmon-phonon polaritons (HP$^{3}$) to probe the dynamical electronic response, we investigate bilayer graphene from AB stacking to $5.5^\circ$ TBG. We identify a narrow density window in which the HP$^{3}$ wavelength becomes strongly gate tunable. The window opens when doping suppresses Landau damping and a coherent graphene plasmon emerges. It closes at a second crossover, which appears only above $4^\circ$ and shifts systematically with twist angle. Continuum-model and electrodynamic calculations trace this second crossover to hybridization between the central and remote moiré bands, which weakens the density dependence of the Drude response. The resulting polaritonic tunability is concentrated within a twist-angle-selected density window and produces total wavelength changes approaching $90\%$. Our results demonstrate that remote moiré bands reshape the collective electrodynamics of TBG far from the magic-angle regime and establish large-angle TBG as a platform for gate-reconfigurable mid-infrared polaritons and material cavities.

title: $AdS$ Leading Regge Trajectory from String Field Theory
summary: We determine the $AdS$ mass of the leading Regge trajectory in superstring backgrounds $AdS_5\times S^5$, $AdS_4\times\mathbb{CP}^3$, and $AdS_3\times S^3\times{\cal M}_4$ with pure Ramond-Ramond (RR) flux for both ${\cal M}_4=S^3\times S^1$ and ${\cal M}_4=T^4$, to the second order in the expansion with respect to the background RR flux by solving the linearized equations of motion in closed superstring field theory. The $AdS_5$ and $AdS_4$ results are in a complete agreement with those obtained from the integrability approach to dual gauge theories, thereby providing a nontrivial check of the holographic duality beyond supersymmetry-protected quantities.

title: Z boson production in lead-lead collisions: An investigation Utilizing MRW nuclear TMDs
summary: We investigate $Z$-boson production in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$ within the $k_t$-factorization framework, using four nuclear transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution (TMD) prescriptions, namely LO-MRW, VO-MRW, MVO-MRW, and MKMRW. The aim of this study is to examine how different ordering conditions and normalization treatments influence the theoretical description of this process. We calculate the rapidity and transverse-momentum distributions using the parton-level KaTie event generator and compare the predictions with CMS measurements and collinear NLO calculations. This comparison allows us to assess the sensitivity of the predicted distributions to the choice of UPDF prescription.

title: Strong hyperbolicity of puncture-gauge formulations of gravitational theories with second order equations of motion
summary: We prove that the modified CCZ4 (mCCZ4) formulation, used in nonlinear puncture-gauge simulations of (d+1)-dimensional Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity and four-derivative scalar-tensor theory in four dimensions, is strongly hyperbolic for both theories at sufficiently weak coupling, provided that the gauge parameters are chosen to satisfy a cone-separation condition. The proof applies to the full principal symbol of the theories, extending previous analyses based on first-order perturbation theory about the Einstein limit. We establish strong hyperbolicity by recasting the mCCZ4 equations into a formally equivalent second-order system whose derivative structure resembles that of the modified harmonic formulation of Kovács and Reall. This allows us to adapt their covariant characteristic analysis and continuity argument, without assuming that individual eigenvalues or eigenvectors depend analytically on the coupling. We also show that standard CCZ4 in general relativity is strongly hyperbolic in puncture gauge away from two defective degeneracies.

title: Localization in one-dimensional magnetic quasicrystals
summary: The celebrated Aubry-André-Harper model undergoes a metal-insulator transition akin to Anderson localization due to an energetic competition between nearest-neighbor hopping and a quasiperiodic on-site potential. In this work, we consider the problem of a one-dimensional lattice subject to a quasiperiodic external field, where the topology of the underlying graph mediates the competition between insulating and conducting phases. In particular, we present examples for which all dispersive eigenstates are critically localized, as well as models in which they are exponentially localized. We also demonstrate the coexistence of these phenomena with an extensive set of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates forming a flat band. Finally, we construct models with exactly solvable mobility edges arising only from graph structure. Going beyond these single-particle results, we show---using exact-diagonalization calculations of the bosonic dynamics---that, as in the conventional Aubry-André-Harper case, on-site interactions drive localized eigenstates toward extendedness. Our results provide a framework for exploring how magnetic interference and interactions jointly constrain transport in quasiperiodic lattices.

title: High-density correlation energy of the electron gas
summary: The high-density expansion of the correlation energy per electron of the unpolarized three-dimensional electron gas, $ε_c = A\ln r_s + B + C r_s\ln r_s + D r_s + \dots$, is used in many approximations to the correlation functional of density-functional theory. The coefficients $A$, $B$ and $C$ are known exactly. We revisit the three diagram classes used to estimate $D$, namely bare rings, rings with one first-order exchange insertion, and third-order diagrams with three distinct momentum transfers. Their sum is $-0.0077880(9)$ Ha per electron, compared with the earlier estimate of $-0.010$ Ha. The difference comes mainly from the coupling-constant weighting of the exchange rings in the calculation of Carr and Maradudin. At order $r_s^2$, seven contributions to the single-logarithm coefficient $E_1$ sum to $(3.653 \pm 0.010)\times 10^{-3}$ Ha per electron. The three long-wavelength contributions to the double-logarithm coefficient $E_2$ sum to $α^2(36π^2 - 208\ln 2 - 221)/(192π^4) \approx -1.433\times 10^{-4}$ Ha per electron, where $α= (4/9π)^{1/3}$. Available diffusion Monte Carlo energies at $r_s = 0.5$ cannot distinguish between the two estimates of $D$.

title: BPS baryonic tubes in chiral perturbation theory minimally coupled with electrodynamics and a novel crossover
summary: We derive a novel first-order BPS system (whose solutions are automatically solutions of the second-order field equations) in chiral perturbation theory (CPT) in $(3+1)$ dimensions. These BPS configurations describe baryonic tubes carrying a chiral current along the tubes themselves. Such baryonic tubes can be either homogeneous or modulated along the $z$-axis. We analyze the leading term in CPT, which is the $SU(2)$ non-linear sigma model minimally coupled to electrodynamics. These exact solutions are qualitatively different from the available analytic description of baryonic tubes since, due to their BPS nature, the positions of the energy-density peaks can be arbitrary. In contrast (in the case of the known solutions in the literature), the energy-density peaks' positions are fixed. We compare these two types of baryonic configurations; the relevant parameter that determines which one is energetically favored is the baryonic charge density: for low densities, the old solutions are favorable, while for high densities these novel BPS tubes are energetically favored. The inclusion of the electromagnetic field (together with the corresponding back-reaction on the baryonic tubes) can also be treated analytically. We discuss the differences in the electromagnetic field distribution between the two regions (low and high baryonic density). The analysis of potential terms for the chiral field is detailed in Appendix B.

title: Z-Boson Production in Proton-Lead Collisions with MRW Nuclear TMDs
comment: 6 pages, contribution to the QCD at the Extremes 2026 proceedings. Summarizes results published in Phys. Lett. B 868 (2025) 139787; see arXiv:2502.16878
summary: The production of dileptons in proton-lead collisions probes the transverse-momentum structure of partons in a nuclear environment. We summarize a $k_t$-factorization study of $Z$ boson production at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=8.16\,\mathrm{TeV}$, comparing transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) distributions constructed with leading-order and Next-to-leading-order Martin-Ryskin-Watt (LO-MRW and NLO-MRW) prescriptions. Parton-level predictions obtained with \textsc{KaTie} are confronted with the CMS measurements in two invariant-mass regions, using the dilepton transverse momentum, $φ^*_η$ and center-of-mass rapidity. The models describe the overall trends near the $Z$ resonance, while the virtuality constraint in NLO-MRW changes the high-transverse-momentum behavior. At lower dilepton masses, both prescriptions underestimate parts of the data, particularly the NLO-MRW result. These comparisons illustrate both the potential and the limitations of last-step-evolution nuclear TMD models for $Z$ boson production in proton-nucleus collisions.

title: Geometrothermodynamics characterization of ABG-AdS black hole immersed by string clouds
summary: Regular black holes, whose singular cores are replaced by smooth geometries sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics, provide a natural setting to study how thermodynamic stability is encoded in spacetime geometry. Conventional stability criteria, however, depend on the choice of thermodynamic potential. Here we develop the quasi-homogeneous geometrothermodynamics of the regular Ayón-Beato--García anti-de Sitter (ABG-AdS) black hole surrounded by a cloud of strings, a Legendre-invariant framework in which no potential needs to be preferred. We show that the entropy, electric monopole charge and AdS radius act as extensive variables obeying a generalized quasi-homogeneity condition, and that the equilibrium manifold then carries three families of thermodynamic metrics. We establish an exact correspondence between response-function anomalies and curvature singularities: the first metric's curvature diverges on the zero-temperature extremal boundary, where the heat capacity vanishes, signaling Davies first-order transitions, whereas the second's diverges precisely where the heat capacity does, pinpointing Davies second-order transitions. The Gibbs free energy displays a swallow-tail structure that reveals a first-order small/large black hole transition, whose metastable region is bounded by these divergences of the heat capacity, together with a Hawking--Page-type transition to thermal AdS. The string-cloud density and the electric charge jointly control the horizon structure, the admissible thermal domain and the stability intervals.

title: The Schwarzschild-Kerr crossover of high overtone quasinormal modes
summary: A slowly rotating black hole is close to a nonrotating one, but its highly damped quasinormal spectrum is not. The Schwarzschild approximation holds only up to overtone numbers of order $χ^{-4/3}$, where $χ$ is the dimensionless spin. We find that the frequency shift at this scale is a universal function, derived from the wave boundary conditions with an error estimate. It is given by the spectrum of a sextic oscillator, via the correspondence between ordinary differential equations and integrable models. It recovers the Schwarzschild $\log 3$ and organizes the singular Kerr coefficients.

title: A fermionic framework for quantum machine learning benchmarks
summary: We present a framework for building and benchmarking scalable machine learning (ML) models based on simulating free-fermion systems. Our fermionic ML (FermiML) framework is (i) versatile enough to encompass kernel methods and neural networks, (ii) applicable to classification and regression, and (iii) scalable to real-world datasets. FermiML models are quantum circuits sharing the building blocks of most quantum ML (QML) models: (parameterized) qubit rotations and entangling gates. This allows us to build fermionic surrogates that mimic the architecture, and hence the quantum resources and inductive bias, of any QML model while remaining efficiently classically simulable. We thus benchmark QML models against close fermionic counterparts on equal footing and ascertain whether a purported QML gain truly stems from classically inaccessible resources or is an accidental side-effect. Across 31 configurations from five classification datasets, we benchmark quantum kitchen sinks (QKS), instantaneous quantum polynomial (IQP) and generic parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) models against fermionic surrogates. fQKS significantly outperforms QKS and is statistically indistinguishable from IQP and PQC; fPQC outperforms IQP and QKS and ties PQC in 28 configurations. We also introduce fermionic fidelity and Pfaffian covariance kernels for regression and establish QML baselines for this harder task. Finally, we introduce a fermionic energy-based classifier scalable to large text and image datasets, which outperforms prominent QML models on images, beats or closely trails them on text, and stays close to classical baselines throughout. Our results show that while performance depends sensitively on architecture, FermiML yields fermionic surrogates that challenge or outperform their unrestricted counterparts and fermionic QML models that match the scale of classical baselines on real-world datasets.

title: Hadron structure in $1+1$ dimensions from the infinite Hamiltonian lattice
summary: The internal structure of a hadron is encoded in matrix elements of operators between hadron states of definite momentum. In this paper, we develop a framework for computing such matrix elements in $(1+1)$-dimensional gauge theories by working on an infinite spatial lattice. We apply the method to the massive Schwinger model. We benchmark our method against discretized lightcone quantization (DLCQ) at $θ= 0$, and then use the lattice to study hadrons at $θ\neq 0$, where DLCQ does not apply. We compute parton distribution functions and gravitational form factors, and both show signatures of hadrons becoming large, loosely-bound states when we set $m$ greater than the critical mass $m_c$ and approach $θ= π$ from below. Moreover, we see the gravitational form factor change from that of a free boson to that of a free Majorana fermion when we set $θ= π$ and approach the 2D Ising critical point at $m=m_c$ from below.

title: Triple-Higgs production: a window on the Higgs potential and anomalous top-Higgs couplings
comment: 20 pages, 8 figures, full-precision parametrisations, MC uncertainties and correlations provided as ancillary files
summary: We present a comprehensive study of triple-Higgs production within the $κ$-framework as a probe of the Higgs potential and anomalous top-Higgs couplings. At leading order, we derive compact parametrisations of the inclusive $gg\to3h$ cross section in terms of the trilinear and quartic Higgs self-coupling modifiers $κ_3$ and $κ_4$, the top-quark Yukawa coupling modifier $κ_t$, and the anomalous two-top-two-Higgs and two-top-three-Higgs coupling modifiers $κ_{2t}$ and $κ_{3t}$. These parametrisations allow for a fast and accurate interpretation of current and future LHC measurements. Applying them to LHC Run 2 data and high-luminosity LHC projections, we quantify the impact of $κ_t$, $κ_{2t}$, and $κ_{3t}$ on the constraints on $κ_3$ and $κ_4$, and derive the first direct constraint on $κ_{3t}$ from existing LHC data. We further show that parameter points yielding nearly identical inclusive rates can give rise to different kinematic distributions, demonstrating the potential of differential measurements to resolve degeneracies and enhance the sensitivity of future triple-Higgs searches.

title: The Cosmological Constant as a Clock and the Vilenkin Wavefunction as a Resonance
summary: We address the problem of time in quantum gravity using a covariant formulation of unimodular gravity. As a result, the cosmological constant is canonically conjugate to a global four-volume variable, which serves as a clock and leads to a time-dependent Wheeler--DeWitt equation. We construct exact, background-independent solutions related to the full Chern--Simons--Kodama state and demonstrate unitary evolution in minisuperspace. The Chern--Simons functional also provides an intrinsic gravitational clock. These solutions reveal that the Vilenkin wavefunction is a gravitational Gamow resonance, in which its non-normalizability follows from the outgoing boundary condition. The tunneling probability into the expanding branch increases with the positive cosmological constant. These results give a dynamical interpretation of the wavefunction of the universe and clarify the role of its boundary conditions.

title: Dynamical phase transition in Brownian motion via sharp large deviations
summary: We prove a dynamical phase transition in Brownian motion with drift, a phenomenon recently predicted in the physics literature. Specifically, when a Brownian motion with drift on a long time interval is conditioned on an upper large deviation event for the (normalized) occupation measure of the interval [-1,1], in the spirit of the Gibbs conditioning principle, a phase transition occurs. If one conditions on a large deviation event in the far upper tail, the conditioned process follows the Langevin diffusion suggested by the Donsker-Varadhan variational formula for additive functionals. In contrast, if one conditions on a large deviation event in the near upper tail, the conditioned process follows a different Langevin diffusion on a fraction of the time interval and subsequently behaves like the unconditioned process. We establish this phase transition via a new sharp large deviation result for the occupation measure, which is of independent interest. We also provide further corollaries of this result and discuss generalizations to other Markov processes and additive functionals.

title: Imaging Compressible and Incompressible Kinetic Energy of a 2d Bose-Einstein Condensate
summary: We introduce a method based on velocity-sensitive two-photon transitions to reconstruct the two-dimensional velocity field as well as the local atomic density of a Bose-Einstein condensate in a single realization. We quantitatively benchmark the method on a quantized vortex. Applied to a condensate far from equilibrium, the method reveals the contrasting behaviors of the system's flow kinetic energy components, where the compressible component quickly decays while the incompressible one remains, dominating the long-time dynamics.

title: A cubic theory of gravity with quasitopological-like properties for compactified cosmologies
summary: We identify a cubic combination of curvature invariants in dimension $D=7$ that when added to the Einstein-Hilbert action, yields a healthy cosmological evolution in four dimensions after compactification on a constant-curvature internal space of dimension three. For generic backgrounds it leads to fourth-order field equations, nevertheless, on a warped product of a spatially flat, homogeneous and isotropic four-dimensional universe with a constant-curvature space of radius $b(t)$, the constraint is of first order in the scale factor $a(t)$ and in $b(t)$, while the remaining equations are of second order. Requiring this property uniquely singles out the cubic theory. We study the solutions describing a four-dimensional de Sitter Universe in direct product with an internal space of stabilized radius and evaluate its linear stability under time-dependent perturbations, showing that for a given sign of the curvature of the internal space, stability of the static solution fixes the sign of the higher curvature coupling. We also argue that linearized scalar perturbations depending on the spatial coordinates obey equations with at most two time derivatives. Finally, we numerically evolve the homogeneous and isotropic system non-linearly and present evidence that for a positive bare cosmological term $Λ_0$ and a hyperbolic compact space, the singularity formation present in GR in this ansatz is pushed into the future by increasing the higher-curvature coupling.

title: Scalar-tensor interactions selected through their first-order thermodynamic dynamics
summary: We investigate the restrictive capability of first-order thermodynamics on scalar-tensor gravity. Starting from a general action containing nonlinear curvature dependence, an Einstein-tensor-Hessian coupling, and independent quadratic and cubic scalar-Hessian interactions, we derive the complete effective-fluid quantities. Simultaneously imposing Eckart's heat-conduction and shear-viscosity equations, while accounting for cancellations between interactions, substantially reduces the original operator basis and determines the geometric shear viscosity. Retaining the complete heat-conduction law, we establish an integrability condition that constrains the nonlinear Hessian interactions without prescribing the temperature and thermal conductivity. We construct explicit constitutive pairs and derive the associated thermal evolution, revealing contributions beyond the usual acceleration-aligned description. Remarkably, the thermodynamic integrability condition simplifies the scalar-metric kinetic structure such that imposing covariant degeneracy excludes the remaining nonlinear interactions, recovering the established luminal Horndeski subclass. Nonlinear thermodynamically compatible interactions nevertheless survive when degeneracy is restricted to the scalar-unitary gauge. These results establish a connection between thermodynamic integrability and dynamical degeneracy, demonstrating the potential of first-order thermodynamics as an independent and complementary criterion for selecting gravitational interactions.

title: Higher-symmetry selection rules for second- and third-harmonic radiation in the Bullough-Dodd model
summary: We investigate nonlinear excitations of the discrete shape mode about a static complex soliton of the integrable Bullough-Dodd model. Extending the linear stability analysis to third order in the excitation amplitude, we construct explicit spatially localised corrections to the shape-mode oscillation and determine its nonlinear frequency shift using the Poincaré-Lindstedt method. Although both the second and third harmonics lie inside the continuous spectrum of the linearised fluctuation operator, the corresponding inhomogeneous equations admit exact localised particular solutions. We demonstrate that the nonlinear sources have vanishing on-shell overlaps with the scattering states at both harmonic frequencies, suppressing the corresponding radiative responses. We further investigate the role of integrability and show how a higher commuting symmetry of the Bullough-Dodd equation provides a perturbative selection-rule interpretation of these cancellations. Our results illustrate how higher integrable symmetries can constrain nonlinear resonances that are otherwise permitted by the linear spectrum.

title: Translation Method Bounds for 3D Isotropic Conductivity--Shear Modulus and the Search for Attaining Microstructures
summary: We compute conductivity--shear-modulus cross-property bounds in three-dimensional isotropic two-phase composites using the translation method, and obtain the tightest bounds reported to date. To assess attainability, we perform unit-cell topology optimization on thousands of distinct initial structures and compare optimized designs to the isotropic bounds using an effective-medium approximation that models the macroscopic material as an isotropic assembly of randomly oriented grains. The best jointly performing designs are consistently bicontinuous, triply periodic minimal surface-like microstructures; however, a small but notable gap to the translation bound remains.

title: Beyond the Thermodynamic-Volume Limit in Holographic Complexity
summary: In the large black hole regime, holographic complexity obeys a thermodynamic-volume scaling law, while the finite-size approach to this limit remains unresolved. In this Letter, we develop an analytic description of finite-size corrections to this scaling for complexity of formation in the complexity=volume (CV) proposal of odd-dimensional equal-spinning Myers-Perry-AdS black holes. We find that the leading finite-size correction retains state dependence that is absent from the limiting thermodynamic-volume law. This correction changes sign at a distinguished Critical Horizon Ratio (CHR), where the generic leading finite-size contribution vanishes and convergence to the thermodynamic-volume law is correspondingly accelerated. We further determine the dimension dependence of the CHR analytically, showing that it approaches a finite nonextremal value at large dimension with a calculable leading finite-dimensional correction. These results show that the finite-size approach can provide a new probe of holographic structure, motivating its exploration across different realizations of holographic complexity and its eventual characterization in the dual field theory.

title: General-relativistic Vlasov disks in external magnetic fields around Kerr black holes
summary: We investigate stationary general-relativistic kinetic models of a collisionless gas around the Kerr black hole immersed in an external magnetic field. The main focus is put on razor-thin disks confined to the equatorial plane, but geometrically thick disks are also briefly mentioned. We consider distribution functions corresponding to constant canonical energy and constant canonical angular momentum of particles within the disk and obtain analytic expressions for the electric current associated with the gas. More general solutions characterized by distribution functions depending on the energy and the angular momentum are obtained assuming the Schwarzschild background metric. In explicit examples, we investigate disks in the Wald magnetosphere, describing an asymptotically uniform magnetic field.

title: Eigenvalue-based computation of Richardson pairing spectra and finite-size thermodynamics
summary: We present a numerical workflow for the reduced BCS Richardson model, combining the eigenvalue-based Bethe equations, Baxter-polynomial reconstruction, and complex root finding. Newton-Raphson iteration solves the nonlinear equations for the eigenvalue-based variables; a linear system yields the polynomial coefficients, and Laguerre iteration with polynomial deflation extracts the rapidities. We apply the procedure to equally spaced, quadratic, and hydrogen-like non-degenerate single-particle spectra as the pairing strength varies. For finite systems, we calculate canonical observables from the complete seniority-zero spectrum and check benchmark spectra against exact diagonalization. In an eight-level, four-pair system with a hydrogen-like spectrum, the heat capacity has two maxima at weak coupling. With increasing coupling, the low-temperature maximum shifts upward and the high-temperature maximum downward; the latter ceases to be a distinct local maximum near $g\simeq0.03515$ in the units used. The equally spaced benchmark instead has a single dominant maximum over the coupling interval displayed for that spectrum. This comparison illustrates how single-particle level spacings can shape finite-size thermal response. The C++ code is publicly available; numerical instabilities remain possible near ill-conditioned configurations and at larger sizes.

title: Strong Co-O exchange interaction in $P4/nmm$ KCoO$_2$ and its effect on spin wave and Néel temperature
summary:
The exchange interactions of a classical Heisenberg Hamiltonian
  in KCoO$_2$ in the $P4/nnm$ structure
  are calculated using a linear response approach, derived from the transverse
  spin susceptibility, integrated over atomic spheres using a projector proportional the local magnetization and including all atoms as magnetic atoms. The exchange interaction between Co and its apical O is found to be by far the largest interaction and ferromagnetic. Its effect on the Néel temperature and the spin wave spectrum are evaluated. The Co-O exchange is found to strongly enhance the critical temperature in the mean field approximation but not in the random phase approximation.

title: NS5-branes and the black hole/string transition
summary: Near to the onset of BTZ black hole formation in string theory is a large ensemble of 6d BPS supergravity solutions sourced by slightly separated fundamental strings and Neveu-Schwarz fivebranes. We extend the construction of these geometries to include gauge excitations of the fivebranes, and then study the energetics of D-string solitons in relation to the deconfinement transition of little strings, which are the natural non-abelian degrees of freedom that deconfine in the transition to the black hole phase.

title: $Φ$asmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction
summary: Quantifying selection effects in gravitational-wave population studies requires millions of costly signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) calculations. We present $Φ$asmaNet, a compact neural architecture for structured tabular regression, with staged spectral refinement as an explicit architectural prior. Learned input tokens are refined through ordered attention-based $Φ$-Stages, each augmented by a $Φ$-Refractor subspace-mixing module, then revisited through gated top-down $Φ$-Feedback. Applied to the 11-dimensional parameters of precessing, higher-mode binary black hole signals (IMRPhenomXPHM), it predicts phase-averaged optimal SNR for a single detector at fixed Advanced LIGO design sensitivity. With approximately 732k parameters, it outperforms MLP, 1D-ResNet and Transformer-encoder baselines under matched training across $10^5$--$10^6$ samples. At $10^6$ samples, it achieves $100-\mathrm{MAPE}=98.73\%$ on the held-out test set, $99.29\%$ after rank-preserving monotonic (PCHIP) calibration, and $99.39\%$ ($R^2=0.9998$) in the detection-relevant regime $ρ>8$, with stable accuracy across independent dataset realizations. On a single GPU, it sustains approximately $1.2\times10^5$ SNR evaluations per second and processes a $10^6$-injection catalogue end-to-end in approximately 8.3 s, about two orders of magnitude faster than conventional waveform-and-inner-product calculations on a 16-core CPU. Exact distance rescaling through $ρ\propto1/d_L$ supports repeated catalogue-wide detectability evaluations. The fully documented pipeline is intended as a reproducible benchmark, while results on public tabular datasets indicate competitiveness beyond gravitational-wave applications. Although demonstrated for a fixed single-detector configuration, the construction supports extensions to detector networks and epoch-specific sensitivities. (Abridged)

title: Absence of $σ$-criticality in Short-Range Spin Glasses
summary: The stability of ground states in the Edwards-Anderson Ising spin glass in dimensions two and higher against perturbations of a single coupling can be quantified through the ``flexibility'' of that coupling in a particular ground state. The property of $σ$-criticality is one in which varying a single coupling can alter the flexibilities of a (strictly) positive density of couplings in an infinite system, and its presence provides a sufficient condition for the presence of multiple ground state pairs. In a previous paper it was shown for the EA spin glass that $σ$-criticality of the first kind, in which the critical droplet of a bond has a positive-density interface with the ground state, was ruled out in any dimension. The remaining possibility, called $σ$-criticality of the second kind, is one in which a bond lies in the critical droplet boundaries of a positive density of other bonds. We show here that this kind of $σ$-criticality is also absent, ruling out altogether the presence of $σ$-criticality in the EA spin glass. While this doesn't resolve the question of multiplicity of ground state pairs, it removes a sufficient condition for its presence. We then propose a rigorous necessary condition for ground state pair multiplicity.

title: Electrical Degradation of Vertical $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Schottky Barrier Diodes Under Au-Ion Irradiation to a Fluence of $1.3 \times 10^7$ cm$^{-2}$
summary: The electrical degradation and time-dependent current behavior of vertical $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) subjected to energetic Au-ion irradiation were systematically investigated. Two successive irradiation exposures were conducted under a constant reverse bias of $-100$ V to evaluate the effects of heavy-ion irradiation on device performance and transient current response. Following irradiation, the devices exhibited degraded forward conduction, increased specific on-resistance, enhanced reverse leakage current, and reduced apparent carrier concentration. During irradiation, pronounced increases in leakage current and transient current spikes were observed. Following each beam termination, the leakage current exhibited an initial rapid decay followed by a slower relaxation process. Single-exponential fitting identified distinct fast and slow relaxation components, while a double-exponential model provided a more comprehensive description of the overall current decay. After the second irradiation exposure, the characteristic time constants of the fast and slow relaxation processes increased from 33.50 to 40.64 s and from 190.35 to 282.29 s, respectively, indicating prolonged recovery dynamics under repeated irradiation. A charge-trapping-based model is proposed to explain the irradiation-induced current enhancement and subsequent fast and slow relaxation processes through modulation and gradual recovery of the effective Schottky tunneling barrier. These findings provide insights into the relationship between heavy-ion-induced electrical degradation and time-dependent current relaxation in $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ SBDs.

title: M5-branes wrapped on topological disks from maximal 7D gauged supergravity
summary: We study new supersymmetric $AdS_5 \times Σ$ solutions for $Σ$ being a topological disk from the maximal gauged supergravity in seven dimensions with $CSO(p,q,5-p-q)$ gauge groups. These gauged supergravities can be obtained from consistent truncations of eleven-dimensional supergravity on $H^{p,q} \circ T^{5-p-q}$. We find a number of solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(2)$ and $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetries from $SO(5)$ and $SO(3,2)$ gauge groups as well as $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetric solutions from $SO(5)$ and $SO(4,1)$ gauge groups. Solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetry preserve $16$ supercharges while the other solutions preserve only $8$ supercharges. Although some of the solutions give a holographic description of the dual $N=1$ SCFTs in four dimensions with finite central charges, most of the solutions describe codimension-2 defects within $N=(2,0)$ theories in six dimensions. For solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(2)$ and $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetries from $SO(5)$ gauge group for which a complete truncation ansatz of eleven-dimensional supergravity on $S^4$ is known, we also uplift the solutions to eleven dimensions and compute the holographic central charge of the dual four-dimensional $N=1$ SCFT with $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetry.

title: The Matrix in Pieces: Complete BFSS Scattering at Finite Rank
summary: As two matrix blocks separate in Banks-Fischler-Shenker-Susskind matrix quantum mechanics, the modes connecting them develop a growing excitation gap. Supersymmetry cancels their leading vacuum energy, so blocks in internal bound states can scatter as composite particles. We prove that these particle channels are asymptotically complete for the physical relative Hamiltonian at each fixed finite rank $N\ge 2$. Because a block can itself break up as its center moves away from the others, the proof must control motion on both scales. Inverse powers of the matrix radius control derivatives along internal flat directions, while the growing gap suppresses excitations between blocks. Propagation estimates then allow us to resolve successive breakups by induction on the block rank. The incoming and outgoing wave operators each have range equal to the absolutely continuous subspace, and the singular-continuous subspace vanishes. The scattering operator is thus unitary when each constituent can occupy any of its internal bound states. For a normalized incoming state of zero-energy constituents, the outgoing probability missing from the zero-energy channels equals the inclusive probability of producing at least one constituent with positive internal energy.

title: Excess noise and electron-phonon energy transfer in Au wires: Length and temperature effects
summary: As a mesoscopic diffusive wire at low temperatures is driven out of equilibrium by a current, excess noise is observed compared to the equilibrium Johnson-Nyquist fluctuations. The expected form of the excess noise varies depending on the relative rates of wire traversal, electron-electron inelastic energy transfer, and electron-phonon inelastic energy transfer. We measure noise as a function of bias current in diffusive Au nanowires on SiO2/Si with lengths ranging from sub-μm to 30 μm and temperatures from 3 K to 50 K, to map out the interplay between charge shot noise and the crossover to electron self-heating and phonon-dominated noise suppression. As expected qualitatively, shot noise is suppressed with increasing wire length and substrate temperature, as electron-phonon scattering is of increasing importance. In long wires, the simple model of electron-phonon energy loss known to be quantitatively effective below a few Kelvin underpredicts the excess noise in the high bias, high temperature limit. This issue is more severe in wires on SiO2/Si than on bare Si, implying that interfacial thermal conduction must be considered in the thermal path even at comparatively high temperatures.

title: Entanglement structure in conformal Y-junctions
summary: We study how entanglement constrains energy transmission in conformal Y-junctions using holographic and free-field models. We define pairwise effective central charges from mutual information as a natural extension of the interface entanglement coefficient. For holographic junctions, we formulate a branched RT prescription and show that the resulting entropies satisfy monogamy of mutual information. We find that the pairwise effective central charge does not always bound the corresponding energy transmission, but a correction involving finite tripartite information restores the bound, with a sharp coefficient determined by limiting saturation. Free-boson and Dirac-fermion junctions also violate the pairwise bound, but the tripartite correction fails because the tripartite information is positive or vanishing, respectively. Analytic limits and numerical results instead support a candidate square-root correction based on L-entropy, which vanishes in the holographic complete-leg prescription considered here. We discuss the possibility of a common multipartite information bound in general conformal junctions.

title: Longitudinal-dither wavefront sensing: Calibration-free measurement of mode mismatch
summary: Mode mismatch between a gravitational-wave detector and the beams injected into it lowers the power stored in the arms and the level of squeezing. Correcting it requires the complex amplitudes of the three second-order modes, measured on a calibrated scale with the cavity on resonance at its operating power. Here we present a method that obtains a signal proportional to the mismatch by moving the beam on the wavefront sensors already used for alignment control. A longitudinal dither of the cavity adds to the resonant mode a reference field, which reaches the sensors through the same signal chains and so calibrates both the scale of this signal and the Gouy phases of the sensors and actuators, with no external calibration. We demonstrate the method on an optical cavity held on resonance in its operating state at input powers of 2 W and 62 W. At 2 W it yields an optical model that agrees with independent measurements in the mode content, and with the layout model in the actuator Gouy phase within its uncertainty of about $1^\circ$. At 62 W the thermally induced change of the eigenmode is decomposed into waist-size and waist-position changes. The method requires only components that every controlled cavity already possesses and enables continuous in situ monitoring of the mode matching in the operating state.

title: Defining the mathematical family tree with a minimal programming language
comment: 33 pages. https://tegmark.org/mathtree includes and interactive MLISP calculator and a detailed atlas of the mathematical theories and structures
summary:
I introduce MLISP, a Turing-complete language with nine single-character commands (a b c d f 0 i j k), and use it to define 88 mathematical structures and a family tree of 65 theories that they model, with three aims:
  Pedagogy: It presents the mathematical structures in a unified way, with standardized presentation tableaus that define them and axiomatized theories that describe them.
  Connections: It highlights how they are related in the family tree via added symbols, axioms, etc. While the full tree is obviously infinite, its lower parts naturally separate into six main branches: the relational branch, the algebraic branch, the logic branch, the number branch, the set branch and the continuum branch.
  Foundations: The definitions, key theorems and models of each entry are verified in Lean. Mathematical structures are defined as equivalence classes of presentations, which in a constructivist spirit are defined in a simple, explicit and self-contained way in standardized presentation tableaus with minimal human baggage. For finite structures, the generating functions are defined by lookup tables. For countably infinite ones, they are instead defined computationally using MLISP, since more complex languages such as Lean are massive overkill for rigorously defining standard arithmetic operations (for example, the program "jibjbfid" defines subtraction).
  An interactive version is available at https://tegmark.org/mathtree. The Lean code is public, also verifies the correctness of MLISP and includes 43% of the theorems from Mathlib 2026-10-11. \end{abstract}

title: Resolvent reconstruction of minimal strings beyond KdV II: D series models
summary: Three-state Potts gravity and tetracritical Ising gravity have the same central charge and the same conformal spectral curve. What distinguishes their amplitudes once a handle or a boundary is added? We answer this question by extending Johnson's differential-equation approach, in the reconstruction form developed in Part I for the reduced KP hierarchies, to D-series minimal strings. Their spatial operator is a pseudo-differential pencil with a nonlocal Pfaffian term, and the classical energy acquires a second pole at zero momentum. Regularity at both poles fixes the quantum corrections uniquely, ordinary string equations supply them, and the ordinary D flows add boundaries in a way that matches the tau function. At genus one the closed free energy follows from the pencil as a sum of logarithms of critical-value velocities. The two theories differ through the origin of the curve, which the D theory counts as two canonical directions, and through the pairing of every point with its reflection. We follow the origin contribution through the free energies to genus three, the one-holed torus and the torus one-point amplitudes, and in the primary range the latter reproduce the formulas conjectured from worldsheet numerics for both series.

title: Tidally Induced Coda: Double Transients from Black Hole-Star Binary Encounters with Massive Black Holes
comment: 12 pages, 7 figures, 2 appendices. Submitted to ApJL. Code: https://github.com/Kkritos/smbh-binary | Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24372716 | Animation of Fig. 2: https://youtu.be/g8_UbibAqKQ
summary: Dense stellar environments surrounding massive black holes (MBHs) provide a natural setting for dynamical interactions that can produce transient electromagnetic and gravitational-wave sources. In particular, the tidal field of an MBH can strongly perturb binaries undergoing close encounters with it, driving their internal orbits to extreme eccentricities. Here, we investigate the outcomes of such interactions for binaries composed of a stellar-mass black hole (BH) and a star. Using direct few-body scattering experiments with the code SpaceHub, we explore hyperbolic encounters between BH-star binaries and MBHs. We systematically quantify the probabilities of different dynamical outcomes as functions of the binary orbital parameters and MBH mass, with particular emphasis on a channel in which the tidally induced eccentricity triggers a micro-tidal disruption event ($μ$TDE), as the star is disrupted by its BH companion, followed by accretion of the stellar debris onto the MBH. We derive fitting formulae for the $μ$TDE cross section and for the time delay between the two resulting flares, finding that the latter can be a few months for an MBH of $10^6\,M_\odot$. These double transients offer a distinctive observational signature of $μ$TDEs. We estimate event rates ranging from a few to $\sim 100\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ within a luminosity distance of $40\,{\rm Gpc}$.

title: SPARK: Spectral Preconditioned Analytic Residual Kolmogorov Arnold Networks for incompressible Navier Stokes equations
comment: 68 pages, 16 figures, 12 tables, to be submitted to Journal of Computational Physics
summary: We propose Spectral Jet KAN (SJ-KAN) to reduce the cost of differentiation and the network complexity of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for the Navier-Stokes (NS) equations. The input coordinates are embedded through Chebyshev bases whose spatial derivatives are known in closed form, and all differentiation matrices are computed once for the collocation points before training. A single linear layer compresses the Chebyshev bases into a few latent features, and a single nonlinear Chebyshev Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (CKAN) layer maps these features to the physical variables. Because the basis derivatives are known in advance and the compression is linear, the spatial derivatives in the NS equations are carried through the network analytically by a fixed sequence of matrix products and elementwise operations. Automatic differentiation (AD) is used only in backpropagation, to compute the gradients of the loss with respect to the network weights. We examine three variants of SJ-KAN (JetKAN, JetKAN-F, JetKAN-H), which differ in how the output layer maps the latent features to the physical variables. All variants are tested on the Taylor-Green vortex and on the lid driven cavity at Reynolds numbers Re = 100, 1000, 5000 and 10,000. The results are compared with a KAN that uses AD (PIKAN) and with a standard PINN. The SJ-KAN variants reach comparable or better accuracy than both, with up to 47 times fewer parameters and up to 8.2 times faster training per epoch. SJ-KAN also solves the lid driven cavity flow at Re = 10,000 without any reference data and with fewer than 9,000 trainable parameters. These results show that analytic derivative propagation, a small spectral input layer and a single KAN layer give a faster and simpler solver than methods based on AD, also for flows at high Reynolds numbers.

title: Density-dependent photocarrier recombination in $γ$-InSe
summary: We studied the photocarrier dynamics in $γ$-InSe using femtosecond transient reflectance spectroscopy. By measuring the dependence of the differential reflectance on the injected carrier density, we established an empirical relation between the optical response and carrier density, allowing quantitative analysis of the recombination dynamics. The carrier decay exhibits a strong density dependence, indicating a substantial contribution from nonlinear recombination. At high carrier densities, the dynamics are dominated by a second-order recombination process, with a rate constant of $3.8\times10^{-6}~\mathrm{cm^3\,s^{-1}}$. At low densities, the decay becomes approximately exponential, with a carrier lifetime of about 7 ps. We also resolved an initial rise of the band-edge response with a time constant of less than 1 ps, which is attributed to hot-carrier cooling. These results reveal the competition between first-order and second-order recombination in $γ$-InSe and provide quantitative insights into its ultrafast photocarrier dynamics.

title: Holographic Entanglement Entropy of Network CFT
summary: Miao et al. \cite{Guo:2025sbm, Guo:2026prm} proposed the AdS/NCFT correspondence, which explores the gravity dual of conformal field theories defined on networks. While previous studies investigated this model within Einstein and Gauss-Bonnet gravity (first- and second-order Lovelock gravity), in this paper, we generalize the framework to higher-order Lovelock gravity and more complex network structures. We derive the extremal and junction conditions for generalized Ryu-Takayanagi (RT) surfaces in third-order Lovelock gravity, which can be naturally extended to arbitrary higher-order Lovelock theories. Focusing on a network model comprising one node and three branches, we numerically investigate the relationship between the network holographic entanglement entropy (HEE) and gravitational coupling coefficients. Furthermore, by analyzing the HEE across various network configurations, we find that the primary structural feature affecting the network HEE is the presence of internal nodes within line-shaped networks. Our results indicate that the network HEE decreases as the number or depth of internal branches increases.

title: The Hidden Simplicity of the Classical Limit
summary: We study the classical limit of two-to-two massive-scalar amplitudes at all orders of perturbation theory. We compute these amplitudes in the probe limit for several theories: a family of scalar theories, electrodynamics, and $\mathcal{N}=8$ supergravity with half-BPS matter. We show that related multiple-emission classical amplitudes obey a simple factorization derivable from the usual factorization of quantum amplitudes. The classical factorization, which reflects the second-order nature of classical dynamics, holds in more general theories --- including gravity. We further show that both the multiple-emission and the two-to-two classical amplitudes have a simple organization in terms of weighted trees. This allows a recursive computation to all orders in the probe limit. The probe's trajectory emerges as a generating function of trees. The required boundary conditions are given by the Feynman $i \varepsilon$ prescription, leading to a novel worldline Green's function. In our approach, the rich classical dynamics arises from simple combinatorics.

title: Spatial switching near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet: a mechanism for multi-bump bound states in coupled nonlinear Schrödinger systems
summary: We study how a localized standing wave of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger (CNLS) system can switch between components from one pulse to the next. The standing wave reduction of the CNLS system yields a four-dimensional Hamiltonian system with two reflection symmetries, in which four elementary pulses correspond to a bouquet of homoclinic loops to a saddle. For saddle eigenvalues $\pmλ_{1},\pmλ_{2}$ satisfying $0<λ_{1} < λ_{2} < 2λ_1$, and under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions, we construct stable and unstable invariant manifolds of the four-loop bouquet. Apart from trajectories asymptotic to the saddle in the corresponding time direction, these manifolds characterize one-sided trapping near the bouquet within the critical Hamiltonian level, namely the level set containing the saddle equilibrium. Both manifolds have codimension one in this level. We prove that if they intersect transversely away from the bouquet, producing super-homoclinic orbits, then there exist infinitely many multi-bump homoclinic orbits to the saddle. These orbits correspond to multi-bump localized standing waves of the CNLS system.

title: Spin Hamiltonian, magnetic anisotropy and excitation spectrum in altermagnetic $α$-MnTe from first principles
summary: The hexagonal altermagnet $α$-MnTe combines a near-room-temperature collinear order with a strongly spin-split electronic structure, yet the microscopic origin of its easy-plane anisotropy, its zone-center magnon gap and its anomalously large magnetostriction have remained unexplained. We derive the complete low-energy magnetic Hamiltonian of $α$-MnTe from first principles, combining density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory with a force-theorem evaluation of the full anisotropic intersite exchange, single-ion terms and classical dipolar couplings. The isotropic exchange, including the altermagnetic splitting of the tenth-neighbor coupling, agrees with inelastic neutron scattering data. Contrary to the common single-ion picture, we find that the easy-plane anisotropy and the magnon gap at $Γ$ are governed by classical dipole-dipole interactions, which enhance the zone-center magnon splitting threefold leading to quantitative agreement with experiment, while the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term is irrelevant despite its size. The same Hamiltonian reproduces the chiral magnon splitting along antinodal directions, mirroring the electronic spin splitting, and quantitatively accounts for the giant magnetovolume coupling of $α$-MnTe through the volume dependence of superexchange.

title: D0-brane bound states in Matrix theory: nonperturbative bounds on matrix extent, noncommutativity and spatial shape
summary:
In Matrix theory, a single eleven-dimensional supergraviton is associated with a BPS bound state of D0-branes. Assuming the existence of a normalized physical BPS state, we derive nonperturbative bounds on its matrix extent, noncommutativity and spatial shape from supersymmetry in the BFSS model.
  The probability of matrix configurations smaller than a fixed fraction of an explicit extent scale is exponentially suppressed in the square of the number $N$ of D0-branes. In Yang-Mills variables, this scale for the trace-normalized extent is of order the cube root of the 't Hooft coupling. Relative noncommutativity, measured by a dimensionless commutator ratio, has an expectation bounded by a quantity of order the inverse of $N$, and its probability of exceeding a sufficiently large fixed multiple of the inverse of $N$ vanishes at large $N$.
  Concentration of the matrix extent along a fixed number of principal directions fewer than nine at large $N$ requires the total extent relative to a corresponding reference scale to diverge in probability. It also requires relative noncommutativity to be suppressed more strongly than the inverse of $N$, in every fixed finite moment of order at least one.
  These bounds apply to the full quantum wave function, including off-diagonal matrix degrees of freedom, and constrain the quantum structure of D0-brane bound states and the possible large-$N$ matrix geometries in Matrix theory.

title: Late-time cosmic acceleration from matter inhomogeneities: constraints from DESI DR2 and SNe Ia
summary: We present the first observational constraints on the Misner-Sharp (MS) mass of the universe, within a newly proposed exact General Relativity solution providing a non-perturbative description of nonlinear cosmic structure formation. At early times, when statistical homogeneity and isotropy are satisfied, our model reduces to usual FLRW cosmology, accommodating Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data. At late times, the departure from homogeneity and isotropy on scales $\lesssim 200$ Mpc -- codified in the scale-dependent redshift distribution of the MS mass -- naturally induces cosmic acceleration, through an extensive term generated by the MS mass asymptotic limit on large scales. We derive the MS mass from Baryon Acoustic Oscillation data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) and Type Ia Supernovae, obtaining a value of the cosmological constant in agreement with $Λ$CDM results. We outline broader implications and future observational prospects, highlighting how multi-probe strategies -- particularly CMB lensing and the late Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect -- can ultimately test this solution to the dark energy puzzle.

title: Upper and lower bounds for the critical point of the three-dimensional Ising model
comment: 37 pages, 6 figures. Code, certificates and logs: https://github.com/whyihaveyou/ising3d-critical-interval (archived at doi:10.5281/zenodo.24487984)
summary: We prove that the critical point $K_c$ of the nearest-neighbour Ising ferromagnet on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ satisfies $0.2164203058<K_c<0.2293910295$, equivalently $1.541630483<e^{2K_c}<1.582145851$, with both endpoints given by explicit rational numbers. To our knowledge these are the sharpest rigorous bounds available. They improve the classical bounds of Fisher (1967) and of Fröhlich, Simon and Spencer (1976), narrowing the rigorously known interval by a factor of about 3.5, and the interval contains the numerical estimate of the critical point. For the lower bound we refine Fisher's self-avoiding-walk argument. A shortest path in the high-temperature expansion forbids all bonds spanned by its vertices, and the resulting gain is estimated through local correlation integrals and summed over paths by a finite-memory transfer bound. As a by-product, the connective constant of $\mathbb{Z}^3$ is shown to be at most $4.73195$. For the upper bound we prove an infrared bound whose coefficient involves the nearest-neighbour correlation. We keep the zero Fourier mode as an unknown and force it to be positive by exact local relations for the spins on a small shell. The finite inequalities entering the proof are verified in exact rational arithmetic, and the passage to the thermodynamic limit is proved analytically.

title: Absence of $σ$-criticality in Short-Range Spin Glasses
summary: The stability of ground states in the Edwards-Anderson Ising spin glass in dimensions two and higher against perturbations of a single coupling can be quantified through the ``flexibility'' of that coupling in a particular ground state. The property of $σ$-criticality is one in which varying a single coupling can alter the flexibilities of a (strictly) positive density of couplings in an infinite system, and its presence provides a sufficient condition for the presence of multiple ground state pairs. In a previous paper it was shown for the EA spin glass that $σ$-criticality of the first kind, in which the critical droplet of a bond has a positive-density interface with the ground state, was ruled out in any dimension. The remaining possibility, called $σ$-criticality of the second kind, is one in which a bond lies in the critical droplet boundaries of a positive density of other bonds. We show here that this kind of $σ$-criticality is also absent, ruling out altogether the presence of $σ$-criticality in the EA spin glass. While this doesn't resolve the question of multiplicity of ground state pairs, it removes a sufficient condition for its presence. We then propose a rigorous necessary condition for ground state pair multiplicity.

title: The DBI critical electric field in stationary non-diagonal geometries
summary: We investigate the critical electric field for the holographic Schwinger effect in general stationary non-diagonal geometries. We show that, in such backgrounds, the DBI reality condition must be formulated in terms of the electric field measured in a local orthonormal frame, since the coordinate components of the field strength need not represent a purely electric field in that frame. The critical field measured in the orthonormal frame takes the universal value \(E_{\mathrm{proper},c}=T_F\), while its coordinate expression depends on the background geometry. The resulting critical field is independently confirmed by the holographic potential analysis, through the disappearance of the potential barrier. We further illustrate the general prescription using the planar limit and the global rotating Myers--Perry--AdS geometry, which exhibit different types of metric mixing.

title: A Kerr-black-hole worldline action to $\mathcal{O}(G^5)$
summary: We establish a worldline action which correctly reproduces Kerr-black-hole dynamics up to fifth order in Newton's constant in a physical post-Minkowskian counting. This encompasses operators up to second order in the Riemann curvature tensor and up to fourth order in the spin tensor. Doing so entails performing the full effective-field-theory computation of the amplitude for a gravitational-wave scattering off of a spinning compact object up to four-loop order, and matching the result to the predictions from linear black hole perturbation theory. Quadratic-in-curvature operators which must be added to match successfully include time-reversal anti-symmetric ones at linear and cubic spin orders, capturing absorption across the black hole horizon, and conservative quadratic-in-spin ones. As an immediate application of our action, we compute the leading-order change in spin magnitude, and reproduce the leading change in mass, for a Kerr black hole in a scattering event with a second compact body, considering a generic orientation of the black hole's spin.

title: Mass gap for finite connections in supercritical percolation
comment: 270 pages with thirteen figures. This paper supersedes arXiv:2408.16636 incorporating much of its content into Part I. The earlier preprint may be consulted for a freestanding proof of a stretched-exponential bound on renewal-block height
summary:
We consider finite open clusters based at the origin in Bernoulli bond percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for $d\geq3$ at a supercritical value $p>p_c(d)$, whose maximal height in the direction of a unit vector $\pmb{\ell}$ lies in a fixed-width window at distance $u$. Conditioned on this event, we prove that, except with probability exponentially small in $u$, such a cluster is populated at positive density by renewal points. Here, a renewal point $w$ is the only vertex of the cluster in the fixed-width band immediately below the height hyperplane through $w$.
  The main technical estimate is that, under this conditioning, the absence of a renewal point is exponentially unlikely. From it we derive an exponential mass gap for the irreducible pieces delimited by successive renewal points, and from the mass gap the stated renewal abundance. The mass gap, together with the renewal decomposition and endpoint estimates established here, yields a sharp point-to-point Ornstein--Zernike asymptotic for finite connectivity, with its Gaussian-type power-law correction. The multiplicative prefactor in this asymptotic is positive and real-analytic, and the associated equidecay and Wulff boundaries are real-analytic and strictly convex.
  The principal innovation of the article is the use of a slide resampling that preserves the conditioned law. The slide acts by cutting the long finite connection at a given $\pmb{\ell}$-height and relocating the upper piece by a random shift. The mass gap is obtained by a delicate analysis of an iterated version of the slide operation along a positive density of attempted heights.

title: Majorana flat bands from mirror-particle-hole antisymmetry
